advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Inspect returncodes of the `git rm --cached` / `git commit` calls in `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit` and surface a `failed`/raise on error instead of unconditionally returning `changed`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:76: `def _git(cwd: str, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess: return run_git_write(cwd, *args, check=False)`
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:617-618: batched `_git(tracker, "rm", "--cached", ...)` return values are never inspected
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:619-627: `_git(tracker, "commit", ...)` return value discarded, then unconditionally returns status `changed`
ABSENCE: no returncode check on the rm/commit calls, unlike a raise that run_ensures would catch (ensures.py:172-176)
advisory.finding: `_untrack_runtime_markers_unit` uses `_git` (which runs with `check=False`) for the `git rm --cached` batches and the `git commit`, so if any of those subprocess calls fail the returncode is discarded and the unit still returns `EnsureOutcome(uid, "changed", ...)`. A failed commit would leave the markers tracked while the sweep records the unit as applied.
scenarios: A pre-commit/hook or unexpected index state makes `git commit` fail; unit reports 'changed', marker written, markers still tracked (self-corrected only on a later sweep since the check is level-triggered).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct migrations.md to say the marker is re-materialized during the (current) default list call, not 'the next default list'.
evidence: docs/migrations.md:91-92: `the reader self-heals the fast-path cache: reduce_all_tickets re-materializes a missing .archived marker for a net-archived ticket on the next default list.`
src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:279-280: `if exclude_archived: _heal_missing_marker(entry_path, state)` runs during the current call
advisory.finding: The migrations.md sentence says `reduce_all_tickets` re-materializes the missing marker 'on the next default list', but `_heal_missing_marker` is invoked inline within the current `reduce_all_tickets` call (line 279-280), so the marker is restored during the same list, not a subsequent one.
scenarios: A reader consulting the migration note to reason about when the marker reappears.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py `len(new_ids) == 2` assertions (lines 181, 245, 257) to 3 (or add `untrack-runtime-markers` handling) to match the grown REGISTRY_IDS.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:66 REGISTRY_IDS now has 9 entries including 'untrack-runtime-markers'
tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py:40 `_ORIGINAL_UNIT_IDS = { env-id, gc-config, merge-ours, gitattributes, gitignore, store-compat }` (6 ids)
advisory.finding: Adding `untrack-runtime-markers` to `REGISTRY_IDS` grows the registry from 8 to 9 (3 non-original units), but tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py still asserts exactly 2 new units (`len(new_ids) == 2`) computed as `set(ensures.REGISTRY_IDS) - _ORIGINAL_UNIT_IDS` where `_ORIGINAL_UNIT_IDS` is a fixed 6-element set. These consumer assertions were not updated and will now fail.
scenarios: Running the integration suite after this migration: test_second_sweep_is_idempotent, test_new_units_are_registered, and test_raising_migration_unit_is_recorded_failed all fail on the count assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Bump the three `assert len(new_ids) == 2` checks to `== 3` in test_ensure_project_mapping.py, consistent with the 8->9 pin updates already made in the store test suites.
